title: AI and Tocqueville at Harvard - TimmermanReport.com
gist: David Shaywitz recounts a Harvard seminar where Harvey Mansfield asked whether AI's impact will be 'democratic' (lifting everyone, compressing differences) or 'aristocratic' (raising the peaks, widening disparities), in Tocqueville's sense. Shaywitz relates it to a pharma R&D AI strategy where his 'make the peaks higher' plan was rejected in favor of upskilling everyone 5%, and argues concentrated, visible wins drive adoption.

themes.theme: Will AI benefits be democratic or aristocratic

themes.theme: Enterprise AI adoption: concentrate vs spread

insights.claim: When building a large pharma R&D AI strategy, Shaywitz proposed concentrating AI resources on a handful of committed individuals and teams already making real progress; the head of R&D Digital and Data and the head of R&D rejected it in favor of elevating everyone's AI skills 5%.
insights.speaker: Timmerman Report
insights.so_what: Large pharma AI programs may default to broad, diluted upskilling over focused bets, slowing visible returns on AI R&D spend.
insights.quote: an approach that would “elevate everyone’s AI skills 5%,” rather than supercharge (gratuitously, in their minds) those who already “got it.”

insights.so_what: When evaluating corporate AI programs, look for concentrated, demonstrable wins rather than broad training metrics.
